name: Five-Star Business Finance Ltd
title: Five-Star Business Finance Ltd - 543663 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consumer/MSME lender Five-Star Business Finance: Q1 FY27 disbursements record INR 1,496 cr and collections improving, but guidance is on credit cost and gross NPA, with cost-to-asset rising and no supply-side capacity signal.

summary.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported a record quarterly disbursement of INR 1,496 crore and AUM of INR 13,722 crore, up 4% QoQ. Asset quality metrics improved modestly: 1+ current book rose to 83.30%, 30+ fell to 12.38%, and the 1.85% credit cost was slightly lower QoQ, while slippages were flat at 0.70%. Management guided to lower credit costs and NPLs in coming quarters, with opex staying flat in FY27 on an employee-cost reset. Q&A focused on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-off run-rate, opex, and the timeline to higher leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Average cost of funds down ~15 bps, spread up 3 bps
Recoveries ~INR 35 crore incl. write-off and NPA settlements (vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Micro LAP (core product)
segments.commentary: Onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); management sees yield settling near 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression over next couple of quarters. Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, targeting 25/50/25 mix across ~INR 3 lakh, ~INR 5 lakh and ~INR 10 lakh tickets.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Launched about two quarters ago; management said focus has been on restoring micro LAP before pushing housing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~20% reiterated; management expects FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7%-1.9%; management said the trend is more likely toward 1.7%. Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at ~1.75%-1.8%.
Gross NPA to fall to sub-3% and a steady-state NPA of ~2.5%; steady-state Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%.
Write-offs for FY27 guided at INR 225-250 crore (~INR 55-60 crore per quarter).
Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% in FY27, moving to 5.25%-5.5% from FY28. Branch additions run-rate ~50-60 per year.
Incremental cost of borrowing guided at ~8.5%; spreads expected flat for next few quarters absent policy action. Repo rate increases are a downside risk.
FY28 credit cost expected at ~1.6%-1.7%. Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters; ROA steady state 6%-6.5% and ROE 18%-20% at ~3x leverage.
Management plans to launch one more product (beyond micro LAP and housing) within ~3-6 months, with details to be shared later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at ~856 after adding ~12 in Q1, mainly in Maharashtra and newer states; FY27 additions expected at ~50-60 branches.
Collections and business functions separated into different verticals; management says this lifted productivity without any change in credit filters.
Liquidity: ~INR 1,850 crore held on balance sheet at quarter end; ~INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and ~INR 450 crore raised in Q1.
Pending ADB tranche (ECB) to be raised, with hedging cost impact; timing to be managed.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the constraint; the slowdown over the past 3-4 quarters came from tighter approvals and deliberate disbursement pacing.
June disbursements were ~INR 670 crore; management expects a new normal of ~INR 600-650 crore per month on average, with intra-quarter seasonality being reduced.
Repeat-customer policy relaxed: top-up offered to best customers instead of requiring full prepayment, which management expects to reduce the repayment rate from ~30% toward 27-28%.
Microfinance overlap with Five-Star customers fell from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (per management, not measured for Q1).
Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI): Where will cost-to-assets settle and when does operating leverage kick in?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth due to competitive employee pay; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% this year, moving to 5.25%-5.5% in steady state from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: Has yield repricing largely finished, and what is the current lending rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Large part of contraction done; onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); a further 10-15 bps compression expected over next couple of quarters, settling near 22.25% after NPA interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah (IIFL): Further Stage 3 flow-through expected, any ARC sales, and rollback rates in early buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: No ARC sales. Slippages expected to trend down; recoveries ~INR 35 crore vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4. Rollbacks ~4-5% in 1-60 DPD buckets and ~2-3% in 61-90 DPD; management frames it as stabilisation, with unique customer collection efficiency key.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): How many more quarters until slippages decline and what is a normalised slippage rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in September, December and March quarters; credit cost trending toward 1.7%. Will wait 1-2 quarters of slippage trend before giving a steady-state slippage number.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What drives the disbursement acceleration (demand, approvals, productivity, geography)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand was never the constraint; earlier slowdown reflected tighter approvals and deliberate pacing. Vertical split of business and collections lifted productivity with no change in credit filters; login and sanction traction strong.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What is the outlook for cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing ~8.5%, leaving room for 20-30 bps further compression on the book; pending ADB ECB tranche carries hedging cost; assumes no repo hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Chandrasekhar Sridhar (Fidelity): Is gold loan growth masking underlying stress via repayments by overlapping customers? Also ticket size and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold loans are fully secured and repayments via gold loans are seasonal; microfinance overlap down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (not measured for Q1). Ticket size mix target 25/50/25 across ~INR 3 lakh, 5 lakh, 10 lakh; one more product within 3-6 months. Spreads to stay flat for next few quarters absent policy action.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Why have repayment rates risen, and how does that reconcile with a rising 3-5 year duration share?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose on stronger collections and a policy change: top-up offered to best customers instead of full prepayment. Repayment rate currently ~30%, expected to trend to 27-28%; behavioural tenor ~4-4.5 years. Management said 85-90% of loans are disbursed on 7-year tenure; the vintage shift reflects seasoning and higher disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Rajiv Mehta (Yes Securities): Trajectory of write-offs, coverage build-back, and FY28 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 write-offs guided INR 225-250 crore, roughly flat at ~INR 55-60 crore per quarter; steady-state write-off view in 2-3 quarters. Overall ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%, whichever mix of Stage 1/2/3. FY28 credit cost ~1.6-1.7%. Growth achieved with no change in credit filters.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Shah (Citi): Steady-state bucket mix and employee cost drivers, attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state: Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%, Stage 3 ~2.5%; current book to reach ~85% by end FY27 from 83.3%; 30+ below 12%. Employee cost rise is salary realignment and incentives for branch staff, not ESOPs. Attrition flat so far; trends in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Expense growth this year and whether 20% loan growth guidance stands?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth ~20-21% YoY, similar to Q1; increments and appraisals already in Q1 base. ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%; write-offs INR 55-60 crore per quarter; 20% AUM growth guidance reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Divyansh Gupta (Latent PMS): Why did debt decline from March, cost of funds for levering up, and timing of D/E of 2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 borrowing was muted as banks awaited results; INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and INR 450 crore in Q1; INR 1,850 crore liquidity held. Guide 8.5% incremental cost. D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters, as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually.

qa_highlights.question: Chirag Fialoke (MS Capital): Are incremental disbursements averaging INR 5-7 lakh, and what is the 60-90 DPD bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Average ticket ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, expected to hold around INR 5 lakh; mix guidance unchanged. Management deferred the 60-90 DPD figure to the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: Darshan Deora (Indvest): Steady-state ROE target, and will yields be raised back given higher collection costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA ~8-8.5% on AUM (7-7.25% on total assets); steady-state ROA 6-6.5% and ROE 18-20% at ~3x leverage. Management says the cost increase will be recovered through lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; the 200 bps cut in Oct 2024 tracked borrowing costs falling from 11%+.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: What was June disbursement and is INR 600-650 crore a monthly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: June disbursements ~INR 670 crore; management is working to reduce intra-quarter seasonality and agreed an average of ~INR 600-650 crore per month is a fair assumption for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Yield compression: onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps decline expected over the next couple of quarters, and NPA interest reversals weigh on yields.

Cost of borrowing: guidance of ~8.5% incremental assumes no repo hikes; a rate increase or ADB ECB hedging costs would hit spreads. Management flagged energy costs and possible regulatory liquidity moves.

Asset quality: slippages flat QoQ at 0.70%; credit cost guidance 1.7-1.9% and gross NPA sub-3% depend on slippages turning down in September, December and March quarters. Write-off run-rate ~INR 60 crore per quarter gives little relief in FY27.
Opex and employee cost: opex growth 20-21% YoY and cost-to-assets ~5.75-6% in FY27; attrition is flat and too early to call, with more competitors entering.
Disbursement sustainability: H1 run-rate of ~INR 600-650 crore per month and reliance on a new product within 3-6 months; leverage target of 2x D/E is 6-8 quarters away.
key_quotes: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR 1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year.
So our request is, can you please keep yourself mute so that the background noise is too much.
So it's not like we are completely removing the DNA of collections from the business people.
Srikanth Gopalakrishnan: Interest reversals on NPAs, Renish.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on disbursements, collections and asset-quality direction, but cautious on the near-term outlook: management hedged on borrowing costs, energy and rate risks, and deferred several data questions (rollback, 60-90 DPD, collection efficiency) to the IR team.

adds.what: ~50-60 new branches expected in FY27 (about 12 added in Q1, mainly Maharashtra)

growth.why: Management reiterated ~20% FY27 AUM growth and guided disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%), backed by a record INR 1,496 crore Q1 disbursement, ~12 branch additions with 50-60 planned for FY27, and a stated demand-not-constraint thesis; order-book or specific capacity backing is limited, so backing is partial.
